method.sv: Ofullständigt forskningsurval. Varje flyg märks Enligt tidtabell eller Dokumenterat genomförd. Tidtabeller belägger inte att flyget gick. Militär-, charter- och privatflyg kräver egna rörelsehandlingar med tider; datumuppgifter utan klockslag animeras inte. Storcirklar och jämn rörelse är illustrationer, även för dokumenterade flyg. Tiderna använder historiska tidszoner och äldre flygplatslägen används vid behov. Saknad data betyder inte ingen trafik.
method.en: Incomplete research sample. Each flight is marked Scheduled or Documented as operated. Timetables do not establish operation. Military, charter and private flights require their own timed movement records; date-only records are not animated. Great-circle paths and uniform motion are illustrations, including for documented flights. Historical time zones and airport sites are used where needed. Missing data does not mean no traffic.

Moderna OurAirports-koordinater används endast som ungefärlig markör för flygplatsområdet, inte en rekonstruerad gate eller referenspunkt från 1986. Det moderna namnet Ruđer Bošković förs inte tillbaka till 1986.
notes.en: Dubrovnik in the Pan Am timetable is mapped to Čilipi, opened for scheduled traffic in1962 according to Hrvatska tehnička enciklopedija. The earlier Gruda site is not used. The airport belongs to Yugoslavia in the1986 classification. Modern OurAirports coordinates are only an approximate airport-site marker, not a reconstructed1986 gate or reference point. The modern Ruđer Bošković name is not applied retrospectively.

Det moderna namnet Ruđer Bošković förs inte tillbaka till 1986.

airports.location_note: Contemporary January 1986 city/airport code checked against the Houston Hobby section. airports.location_note: Contemporary January 1986 city/airport code checked against the Houston Hobby section. Airport history and approximate airfield location checked; not a reconstructed 1986 gate, runway threshold or actual aircraft position.

airports.name: Denver–Stapleton International (1986)
airports.location_note: Contemporary January 1986 city/airport identity and historical location reviewed. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions. DEN means Stapleton, closed in February 1995. Uses the closed airfield record US-12484 rather than current Denver International/KDEN.

airports.name: Las Vegas–McCarran International (1986)
airports.location_note: Contemporary January 1986 city/airport identity and historical location reviewed. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions. The current coordinate record says Harry Reid; the historical display name is McCarran. The name change does not relocate the airfield.

airports.name: Ontario International, California
airports.location_note: Contemporary January 1986 city/airport identity and historical location reviewed. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Kansas City International
airports.location_note: Kansas City International/MCI opened for commercial service in November 1972. Distinct from downtown MKC. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions; the 2023 terminal is not represented.

airports.name: Chicago Midway
airports.location_note: Chicago Midway, separate from Chicago O’Hare/ORD. Airport history and the operator’s retrospective identify this airfield and Southwest service since March 1985. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Fort Lauderdale–Hollywood International
airports.location_note: FLL, distinct from Miami/MIA. Contemporary Delta airport-code page 260 identifies Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International. Broward County records document the existing airport terminal expansion during 1985–1987. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Fort Myers–Southwest Florida Regional (1986)
airports.location_note: The contemporary Delta code table on page 261 assigns RSW to Fort Myers Regional. This airfield opened in May 1983; Page Field/FMY is a different airport. Historical 1986 Regional name retained; the newer terminal opened in 2005. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Jacksonville International
airports.location_note: The contemporary Delta code table on page 260 identifies Jacksonville International. Airport authority history establishes the current airport opened in 1968, replacing Imeson; Imeson is not used. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Orlando International
airports.location_note: MCO identified as Orlando International on contemporary Delta page 261. Airport authority history describes international status/name in 1976 and the 1981 terminal complex; separate Orlando Executive/ORL is not used. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: West Palm Beach–Palm Beach International (1986)
airports.location_note: PBI and International are printed for West Palm Beach on Delta page 261. Historical 1986 PBI code/name retained despite the current coordinate record using a later name/code. Airport history describes 1966 and 1974 terminals on this airfield; the 1988 terminal is not represented. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Baltimore–Washington International (1986)
airports.location_note: Contemporary Delta airport-code page 260 identifies Baltimore-Washington International/BWI. Separate Baltimore schedule heading used, not Washington National/DCA or Dulles/IAD. Airport authority history traces this airfield to Friendship Airport, dedicated in 1950; the later Thurgood Marshall name is not applied to 1986. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Hartford/Springfield–Bradley International
airports.location_note: Contemporary Delta airport-code page 260 identifies Hartford/Springfield Bradley International/BDL. Airport authority history identifies the Windsor Locks airfield, military from 1941 and commercial from 1947. Separate Hartford-Brainard/HFD is not used. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: New York–LaGuardia
airports.location_note: Contemporary Delta airport-code page 261 and New York schedule suffix L identify LaGuardia/LGA, separate from JFK and Newark. Port Authority history identifies the Queens airport opened in 1939, with the Central Terminal Building replaced in 1964. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Newark International (1986)
airports.location_note: Contemporary Delta airport-code page 261 identifies Newark International/EWR; New York schedule suffix E denotes this airport. The search-indexed history in the Port Authority report identifies the Newark airfield opened in 1928 and its Central Terminal Area opened in 1973. Full history PDF was not downloaded; the later Liberty name is not applied to 1986. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Greater Pittsburgh International (1986)
airports.location_note: Contemporary Delta airport-code page 261 identifies Greater Pittsburgh International/PIT. Search-indexed airport-authority history distinguishes PIT, constructed in 1952, from Allegheny County Airport/AGC, the earlier commercial airport. Full history PDF was not downloaded; terminal positions are not reconstructed. Approximate airfield coordinates, not reconstructed 1986 gates, runway thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International (1986)
airports.location_note: The February 1986 timetable identifies Toronto as YYZ / Lester B. Pearson International on printed page 261. Airport authority history confirms the continuing site; current coordinates are approximate airfield markers, not reconstructed 1986 gates, thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Cleveland / Cleveland Hopkins International (1986)
airports.location_note: The February 1986 timetable identifies this city and airport code on printed page 260. Airport authority history confirms the continuing site; current coordinates are approximate airfield markers, not reconstructed 1986 gates, thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Dayton International (1986)
airports.location_note: The February 1986 timetable identifies this city and airport code on printed page 260. Airport authority history confirms the continuing site; current coordinates are approximate airfield markers, not reconstructed 1986 gates, thresholds or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Memphis International
airports.historical_location_note: 1986 Memphis International Airport. Airport history establishes continuity of the 1963 terminal and subsequent concourse expansion. Modern FAA aerodrome reference point is used only as an approximate map position, not an exact 1986 runway, terminal or aircraft position.

airports.name: Jackson–Allen C. Thompson Field (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Commercial airport opened in 1963, replacing Hawkins Field. Contemporary 1963 postcard identifies Allen C. Thompson Field/Jackson Municipal Airport. Modern coordinates are an approximate map location for the same airport site, not reconstructed 1986 runway, terminal or aircraft positions. The later Medgar Evers name is not used for 1986.

airports.name: Shreveport Regional
airports.historical_location_note: Commercial service moved from Downtown to the present western airport site in 1952; Shreveport Regional name adopted with the 1971 terminal. Modern coordinates are an approximate map location for the same airport, not reconstructed 1986 runway, terminal or aircraft positions.

airports.name: Louisville–Standiford Field (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Commercial flights moved from Bowman Field to Standiford Field in 1947. A new landside terminal opened in 1985; the airside terminal opened in 1989 and the International name dates to 1995. Modern coordinates provide an approximate airport-area marker only: later runway reconstruction means this is not a precise 1986 runway, gate or aircraft position.

airports.name: Lexington–Blue Grass Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: The airport authority master plan, printed pp1-3 and 1-4, describes acquisition of the Versailles Road site in 1940, construction from 1941 and commercial service from 1946. Blue Grass Field was renamed Blue Grass Airport in 1984. The terminal opened in 1976. Modern coordinates are an approximate marker for that airport site, not a precise 1986 runway, gate or aircraft position.

airports.name: Nashville–Berry Field (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Nashville Metropolitan Council resolution RS2022-1582 describes Berry Field opening in 1937, the later terminal opening in 1987 and the Nashville International name adopted in 1988. The historical Berry Field name is retained. Modern OurAirports coordinates are an approximate airport-area marker, not a precise 1986 terminal, gate, runway or aircraft position.

airports.name: Knoxville–McGhee Tyson Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: The Metropolitan Knoxville Airport Authority master plan executive summary (2006), printed pages 2–3, identifies purchase of the present airport site in 1935, distinct from the earlier West Knoxville airport. Modern OurAirports coordinates are an approximate airport-area marker, not a reconstruction of a 1986 terminal, gate, runway or aircraft position.

airports.name: Chattanooga–Lovell Field (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: The airport authority history identifies the present Lovell Field site as opened in 1930, distinct from earlier Marr Field. It also dates the earlier terminal to 1964 and the later passenger terminal to 1992. Modern OurAirports coordinates are an approximate airport-area marker, not a reconstruction of a 1986 terminal, gate, runway or aircraft position.

airports.name: Greater Buffalo International Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: The airport authority history identifies the Cheektowaga site, acquired in 1925 and opened in 1926, and the Greater Buffalo International name from 1959. The present terminal and Buffalo Niagara name date from 1997, after the imported period. Modern OurAirports coordinates are an approximate airport-area marker, not a reconstruction of a 1986 terminal, gate, runway or aircraft position.

airports.name: Akron–Canton Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: The airport authority history identifies the Summit County site south of Greensburg–Greentown Road, dedicated in 1946; airlines moved here from the separate Akron Municipal airport in 1948. This marker represents CAK, not Akron Fulton/AKC. Modern OurAirports coordinates are an approximate airport-area marker, not a reconstruction of a 1986 terminal, gate, runway or aircraft position.

airports.name: Evansville Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: The airport authority draft master plan introduction (July 2023), printed pp1-4–1-5, identifies the airport built in 1928 along US41 in northern Vanderburgh County. Its later ten-gate terminal opened in 1988 and is not projected back to 1986. Modern OurAirports coordinates are an approximate airport-area marker, not a reconstruction of a 1986 terminal, gate, runway or aircraft position.

airports.name: Monroe Regional Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: The airport authority history connects the present airport with Selman Field and records transfer of the property to the City of Monroe in September 1949. The February 1986 Delta airport directory, printed p261, identifies MLU as Monroe Regional. Modern OurAirports coordinates are an approximate airport-area marker, not a reconstruction of a 1986 terminal, gate, runway or aircraft position.

airports.name: Mobile – Bates Field Municipal (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: The airport authority distinguishes relocated Bates Field in West Mobile from Brookley. The 1986 Delta directory p261 labels MOB Bates Field Municipal. Current KMOB coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not a reconstructed 1986 terminal or runway.

airports.name: Pensacola Regional / Municipal Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: The airport history names this site Pensacola Regional from 1972; the 1986 Delta directory p261 uses Municipal. International is a later name. Current KPNS coordinates are an approximate airport-area marker, not a reconstructed 1986 terminal or runway.

airports.name: Baton Rouge Metropolitan Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: The airport authority identifies the current site as former Harding Field, opened to civilian use in 1948. Delta directory p260 identifies BTR as Metropolitan. Current coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not a reconstructed 1986 terminal or runway.

airports.name: Birmingham Municipal Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies Birmingham Municipal. The airport authority describes the airport opened in 1931 and renamed International in 1993, then Shuttlesworth in 2008. Current coordinates mark the approximate historical airport area, not a reconstructed 1986 terminal or runway.

airports.name: Montgomery Dannelly Field (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies Dannelly Field. The airport authority records its opening in 1943 and air service from 1946, later renamed Montgomery Regional. Current coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not earlier Gunter/Maxwell fields or a reconstructed 1986 terminal/runway.

airports.name: Fort Walton Beach–Okaloosa County Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies Fort Walton Beach as Okaloosa County. The airport authority records the Okaloosa County Air Terminal on State Road 85 opening in 1975 on the Eglin airfield. Current coordinates mark the approximate shared airport area; not Destin Executive (DTS), nor a reconstructed 1986 terminal/gate/runway. The modern Destin-Fort Walton Beach name dates to 2015.

airports.name: Fort Smith Municipal Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 calls FSM Municipal. Airport history records the 1959 terminal, late-1970s expansion and a 1986 runway extension at this site; renamed Regional in 1992. Coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not the 2002 terminal or reconstructed 1986 gates.

airports.name: Columbus–Golden Triangle Regional Airport
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies Columbus, Mississippi as GTR / Golden Triangle. Airport authority history documents construction from 1969 and development before 1986. This is the regional commercial airfield, not Columbus Air Force Base or Columbus-Lowndes County airport. Modern coordinates are approximate airport-area markers.

airports.name: Greenville–Municipal / Mid Delta Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies GLH as Greenville Municipal. Federal Register 30 October 1969 p17511 locates Greenville Municipal at 33°29′05″N 90°59′20″W, the present Mid Delta airfield area. City history identifies the facility as former Greenville Air Force Base. Approximate modern airport coordinates are used; the former separate southeast municipal field is not substituted.

airports.name: Meridian–Key Field
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies Meridian as MEI / Key Field. National Park Service documents the airport complex opening in 1930 and surviving buildings at Key Field. This is the civilian airfield, not Naval Air Station Meridian or Bonita Field. Modern coordinates mark the approximate airport area.

airports.name: Laurel/Hattiesburg–Pine Belt Regional Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 explicitly names PIB Pine Belt Regional for Laurel/Hattiesburg. Historical society records service beginning in 1974 and renaming as Hattiesburg-Laurel in 1990. Coordinates mark the regional field at Moselle, not Laurel Hesler-Noble (LUL) or Hattiesburg Municipal (HBG); no exact 1986 terminal reconstruction.

airports.name: Tuscaloosa Municipal Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies TCL as Tuscaloosa Municipal. The city airport history describes municipal acquisition at the end of World War II and continued use of the same airfield. Modern coordinates mark the approximate airport area; the present National name is not presented as the 1986 name. No precise 1986 terminal, gate or runway reconstruction.

airports.name: Valdosta Regional Airport
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies VLD as Valdosta. Airport authority history places this public airport south of Valdosta, converted from a Moody auxiliary field in 1946, with Atlanta commuter service beginning in 1980. This is the civilian regional airfield, not Moody Air Force Base itself. Modern coordinates are approximate airport-area markers, not reconstructed 1986 gates or terminals.

airports.name: Fayetteville – Drake Field
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies Fayetteville, Arkansas (FYV) as Drake Field. City history places this field at its present site since 1936 and records decades of commercial service. This is not Fayetteville, North Carolina (FAY), nor the later Northwest Arkansas airport (XNA). Modern coordinates are approximate airport-area markers, not reconstructed 1986 terminals or gates.

airports.name: Albany – Dougherty County Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Contemporary Delta directory p260 identifies ABY as Albany, Georgia, Dougherty County Airport. Current city airport page https://airport.albanyga.gov/Airport-Guide/About-ABY identifies KABY as Southwest Georgia Regional at Newton Road. The mapping to the modern field is an identity inference from these records, not a reconstructed 1986 terminal location. Modern coordinates mark the approximate airport area; the period directory name is retained. This is not Albany, New York (ALB).

airports.name: Brunswick – Glynco Jet Port (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies BQK as Brunswick, Georgia, Glynco Jet Port. Airport commission history records civilian opening in 1975 and ASA service to Atlanta from 1981. The present Golden Isles name dates from 2003; the period name is retained. This is the mainland airport, not McKinnon Field on St Simons Island (SSI). Modern coordinates mark the airport area, not a reconstructed 1986 terminal or gate.

airports.name: Gainesville Regional Airport
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies Gainesville, Florida (GNV), Regional Airport. Airport history records the field passing to the city in 1948 and adoption of the Regional name in 1977. This is Gainesville, Florida, not Gainesville, Georgia or Texas. Modern coordinates are approximate airport-area markers, not reconstructed 1986 terminals or gates.

airports.name: Asheville Regional Airport
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies AVL as Asheville, North Carolina, Regional Airport. Airport authority history dates the new airport to 1961, replacing the separate Asheville-Hendersonville field. The 1986 marker uses this Regional airport site. Modern coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not a reconstructed 1986 terminal, gate or runway.

airports.name: Dothan–Houston County Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies DHN as Dothan-Houston County. The airport history records commercial relocation to former Napier Army Airfield in February 1965. This marker uses that field, not the earlier city airport at present Westgate Park. Modern coordinates mark the airport area, not a reconstructed 1986 terminal or gate.

airports.name: Huntsville–Madison County Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies HSV as Huntsville-Madison County. Port of Huntsville history dates the present airport site to October 1967. This is the airport west of the city, not an earlier Huntsville airfield. Modern coordinates are approximate airport-area markers, not reconstructed 1986 terminals, gates or runways.

airports.name: Augusta – Bush Field (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies Augusta, Georgia, AGS as Bush Field. Airport history links this site to service since 1941 and records the Augusta Regional name change in 2000. The period name is retained. This is Bush Field, not Daniel Field (DNL). Modern coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not reconstructed 1986 terminals, gates or runways.

airports.name: Columbus Metropolitan Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies Columbus, Georgia, CSG as Columbus Metro. The airport commission history records Delta jet service from 1968 and a later terminal in 1991. The marker identifies this civil airport, not Columbus Ohio (CMH), Columbus Mississippi (GTR), or Lawson Field. Modern coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not a reconstructed 1986 terminal or gate.

airports.name: Macon Municipal Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies MCN as Macon Municipal. Airport history links the present Middle Georgia Regional field south of Macon to Cochran Field and postwar municipal airline service. The period directory name is retained. This is MCN, not the separate downtown Smart Field/Macon Downtown airport (MAC). Modern coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not a reconstructed 1986 gate or terminal.

airports.name: Panama City–Bay County Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies PFN, Panama City Florida, as Bay County. The airport authority confirms that ECP replaced PFN on 23 May 2010 at a new site. The OurAirports closed-airport record US-9348 identifies the former PFN/KPFN site. These coordinates mark the approximate old airport area, not modern ECP or reconstructed 1986 gates/runways.

airports.name: Greenville–Spartanburg Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies GSP as Greenville/Spartanburg. The airport history records the shared airport opening at Flatwood in 1962, replacing separate city airports. This marker is GSP near Greer, not Greenville Downtown (GMU), Spartanburg Downtown (SPA), or Greenville Mississippi (GLH). Modern coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not a reconstructed 1986 gate or terminal.

airports.name: Anniston–Calhoun County Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies ANB as Anniston Calhoun County. The FAA record reproduced by AirNav lists activation in March 1941 and the civil field southwest of Anniston. University of Alabama aerial-photo inventory lists Anniston Metropolitan Airport from 1957 onward. This is ANB, not ASN/Talladega or Fort McClellan. Modern coordinates are approximate airport-area markers, not reconstructed 1986 terminals or gates.

airports.name: Gadsden Municipal Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies GAD as Gadsden Municipal. The FAA record reproduced by AirNav lists activation in January 1944 and the site southwest of Gadsden, now Northeast Alabama Regional. This is the postwar municipal field, not the earlier Gulf/Republic Steel airfield. Modern OurAirports coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not reconstructed historical gates or runways.

airports.name: Roanoke Regional–Woodrum Field (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 still calls ROA Municipal. The airport history confirms continuity at the Cannaday Farm site, the 1983 Regional/Woodrum name, and a new terminal completed only in 1989. The marker is the same airport area, not a reconstruction of that later terminal or the 1986 gates.

airports.name: Tri-City Regional Airport, Tennessee (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies TRI as Tri-City Regional. City of Kingsport Archives documents McKellar Field opening in 1937 and historic aerials of the shared regional airport. This is the Blountville field serving northeast Tennessee and southwest Virginia, not Tri-Cities/Pasco PSC in Washington. Modern coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not reconstructed 1986 gates.

airports.name: Tallahassee Municipal Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies TLH as Municipal. City audit #1620, printed p10/PDF p15, states the new airport site opened in 1961, replacing Dale Mabry Field, and a new adjacent airline terminal opened in 1989. The marker uses the airport area established in 1961, not Dale Mabry Field or a reconstructed 1986 terminal/gate. Tallahassee uses Eastern Time.

airports.name: Muscle Shoals Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies MSL as Muscle Shoals. TVA's history documents its original 1937 hangar still within today's Northwest Alabama Regional Airport. Together these support continuity of the airport area. Modern coordinates are approximate site markers, not reconstructed 1986 terminals, gates or runway layouts.

airports.name: Richmond–Byrd International Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies Richmond RIC as Byrd International. The airport's own history traces today's field to Richard E. Byrd Airport opened in October 1927. These sources support continuity of the airport area. Modern coordinates are approximate site markers, not reconstructed 1986 terminals, gates or runway layouts.

airports.name: Raleigh–Durham Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies RDU as Raleigh/Durham. RDU's official history traces the current airport terminal area to its 1955 building and adjacent 1982 terminal; the American hub opened only in 1987. This supports continuity of the airport site, not a reconstruction of 1986 gates or later terminals. Modern coordinates mark the approximate airport area.

airports.name: Charleston–Yeager Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies Charleston WV / CRW as Kanawha County. The airport's official history identifies the Coonskin Ridge field opened as Kanawha Airport in 1947 and renamed Yeager in 1985. This is Charleston West Virginia, not Charleston South Carolina CHS. Modern coordinates are approximate airport-area markers, not reconstructed 1986 gates, terminals or runway layouts.

airports.name: Huntington/Ashland–Tri-State Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies HTS as Huntington/Ashland, Tri-State. Airport master plan March 2014, section 1.2.2 / p1-6, identifies the current field opened in 1952 and terminal dedicated in 1961, expanded in 1979. Earlier Kyle Field and Lawrence County Airpark are separate sites. Coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not 1986 gates or runway layouts.

airports.name: Fayetteville–Grannis Field (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p260 identifies Fayetteville/Fort Bragg NC as FAY, Grannis Field. City airport history distinguishes the old Raleigh Road field from the current site opened in 1949; Concourse B opened only in March 1987. This is not Fayetteville Arkansas FYV or military Pope Field. Coordinates mark the approximate airport area, not later terminal additions or 1986 gates.

airports.name: Norfolk International Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta directory p261 identifies Norfolk/Virginia Beach/Williamsburg as ORF, International. Official airport history identifies the current site opened in 1938, new terminal operation from January 1974 and International renaming in January 1976. Not Norfolk naval airfield or Newport News. Coordinates are approximate site markers, not reconstructed historical gates.

airports.name: Charleston International Airport (1986)
airports.historical_location_note: Delta airport directory identifies Charleston, South Carolina, CHS, International. Joint Base Charleston's historical report describes the civilian airport authority taking over operation in 1979 and the new civilian terminal opening in April 1985 on this airfield. notes.sv: Utgåva 11 februari–26 april 1986, delvis transkriberad. Urval från Berlin, Europa, Atlantflyg och Västafrika. Senaste omgången kompletterar fysiska delsträckor via Bryssel, Amsterdam och Hamburg. Marsändringar och mellanlandningar granskas separat. Istanbul-raderna är kandidater på grund av en konflikt i den tryckta tidszonen. Tidtabellen belägger inte faktiskt genomförande eller last. Omgång 18 kompletterar Sydamerika, Venezuela, Trinidad och Tobago samt Mexico City med tidsatta fysiska delsträckor. Importen är avgränsad till 26 februari–1 mars; PA217 till 28 februari. Aprils nya nordiska linjer ingår inte. V55: tre Nonstop-rader ger PA67 Warszawa–Frankfurt lördag, PA76 Budapest–Dubrovnik fredag och PA77 Dubrovnik–Budapest lördag. Båda Dubrovnik-radernas No Local Traffic-anmärkning bevaras. Apriländringar används inte i februari/marsfönstret. München–Budapest:s TuWe och Budapest–München:s WeTh utvidgas inte från anslutningsresors veckodagar. Prag i expansionsannonsen gäller från 27 april och importeras inte. V56: PA77 Zagreb–München-Riem fredag 09:30–10:25 och PA76 München-Riem–Zagreb lördag 11:15–12:10 tillkommer från egna Nonstop-rader. Raderna upphör efter 28 respektive 29 mars. Belgrad–München och retur med ett stopp delas inte utan fullständiga mellantider. Zagreb–Frankfurt:s fredagsvariant från 1 april och Bukarest-rader utanför rätt veckodagar importeras inte. V57: PA61 Aten–Frankfurt fredag 09:30–11:25 och PA150 Frankfurt–Aten lördag 12:15–16:00 tillkommer. Båda är Nonstop med No Local Traffic On Above Flight. UTC+2 i Aten och UTC+1 i Frankfurt ger 175 respektive 165 minuter. Raderna upphör efter 28 respektive 29 mars. Söndagsraden PA151 och senare mars-/aprilvarianter importeras inte. V122: 25 separat tidsatta nonstop-rader i Centralamerika och Karibien ger 51 rörelser. Dagändringar kring 1 mars kontrollerade. Genomgående resor via St. Croix, St. Maarten, Barbados eller Miami blir inte extra direktflyg. Regional täckning är partiell. V123: 9 nya separat tidsatta karibiska nonstop-rader; datumvillkor och Paris A=CDG/S=Orly kontrollerade. Tidtabell, inte bekräftad drift.
notes.en: Edition 11 February–26 April 1986, partly transcribed. Selected Berlin, European, transatlantic and West African services. The latest batch completes physical legs via Brussels, Amsterdam and Hamburg. March amendments and stopovers are reviewed separately. Istanbul rows remain candidates because of a conflict in the printed time-zone heading. A timetable does not establish actual operation or cargo. Batch 18 adds timed physical segments for South America, Venezuela, Trinidad and Tobago, and Mexico City. Import is limited to 26 February–1 March; PA217 to 28 February. New Nordic services starting in April are excluded. V55: three Nonstop rows yield PA67 Warsaw–Frankfurt Saturday, PA76 Budapest–Dubrovnik Friday and PA77 Dubrovnik–Budapest Saturday. Both Dubrovnik rows retain No Local Traffic restrictions. April changes are not applied to the February/March window. Munich–Budapest TuWe and Budapest–Munich WeTh are not expanded using connecting-itinerary day patterns. Prague in the expansion advertisement is effective27 April and is not imported. V56: PA77 Zagreb–Munich-Riem Friday 09:30–10:25 and PA76 Munich-Riem–Zagreb Saturday 11:15–12:10 added from separate Nonstop rows. The rows are discontinued after 28 and 29 March respectively. One-stop Belgrade–Munich itineraries are not split without complete intermediate timings. The Zagreb–Frankfurt Friday variant effective 1 April and Bucharest rows on other weekdays are not imported. V57: PA61 Athens–Frankfurt Friday 09:30–11:25 and PA150 Frankfurt–Athens Saturday 12:15–16:00 added. Both are Nonstop with No Local Traffic On Above Flight. UTC+2 in Athens and UTC+1 in Frankfurt yield 175 and 165 minutes. Rows end after 28 and 29 March respectively. Sunday PA151 and later March/April variants are excluded. V122: 25 separately timed Central America/Caribbean nonstop rows yield 51 movements. Day changes at 1 March checked. Through itineraries via St. Croix, St. Maarten, Barbados or Miami are not extra nonstop flights. Regional coverage remains partial. V123: 9 new separately timed Caribbean nonstop rows; date conditions and Paris A=CDG/S=Orly checked. Timetable, not confirmed operation.

notes.en_source: Tidtabell från 1 februari 1986, delvis visuellt granskad. Importen omfattar Atlantas Europalinjer med retur samt utvalda inrikes nonstopavgångar från Atlanta. Tryckta veckodagar och framtida startdatum är granskade; Orly och Gatwick används. Slutdatum för hela utgåvan är inte fastställt; importerade rader är avgränsade till granskningsperioden 26 februari–1 mars. Tidtabellen visar planerad trafik, inte faktiskt genomförande. V64: ytterligare inrikes nonstopavgångar från Atlanta granskade på tryckta s. 14–18, med teckenförklaring s. 4 och utvalda flygnummer i linjeförteckningen s. 262–264. 123 källrader: 87 nya scheman, 33 tidigare importerade, två rader med otydliga minutangivelser hålls utanför och en rad börjar först 2 mars. 185 nya rörelser till 23 flygplatser. DL137 är fredagsflyg med särskilt giltighetsintervall 28 februari–7 mars; endast 28 februari importeras. DL25 till Honolulu flyger inte måndagar/fredagar. DL790 och DL760 till Detroit kontrollerade i linjeförteckningen. Houston I/H skiljer Intercontinental från Hobby. Returtrafik, fler inrikesorter, anslutningsbolag och ändringsblad återstår. Alla tidigare Delta-rader och rörelser är oförändrade. V65: Atlanta till/från Fort Lauderdale, Fort Myers, Jacksonville, Orlando och West Palm Beach. 72 källrader på tryckta s. 15, 17, 18, 81, 84, 115, 182 och 247; 67 nya nonstop-scheman ger 137 rörelser. Tre genomgående rader med ett stopp, en söndagsvariant och DL158 med start 2 mars hålls utanför. DL94 Orlando–Atlanta har sista trafikdag 1 mars enligt fotnot 14 på s. 183. Flygplatskoder verifierade på s. 260–261. Fem flygplatser tillkommer med granskad historisk identitet. Alla tidigare scheman och rörelser är oförändrade. V66: Atlanta till/från Baltimore, Bradley/Hartford, LaGuardia, Newark och Pittsburgh. 56 källrader på tryckta s. 14, 15, 16, 17, 22, 100, 173 och 195; 55 nya nonstop-scheman ger 123 rörelser. Anslutningsraden DL106/1658 Atlanta–Bradley via LaGuardia hålls utanför som obruten sträcka. New York-suffix L=LaGuardia och E=Newark läses per rad. Flygplatskoder kontrollerade på s. 260–261. Fem flygplatser tillkommer med granskad historisk identitet. Alla tidigare scheman och rörelser är oförändrade. V67: Returtrafik till Atlanta från Boston, Chicago O’Hare, Dallas/Fort Worth, Detroit, Miami, Philadelphia, Tampa och Washington National. 80 källrader på tryckta s. 31, 46, 64, 73, 150, 191, 229 och 244: 59 nya scheman ger 123 rörelser; 12 befintliga rader matchas utan nyimport, fem genomgående rader och två anslutningar utesluts, två lördagsavgångar ligger efter fönstret. DL138 DFW–ATL flyger lördag, med giltighet 1–8 mars enligt fotnot 5 på s. 65; bara 1 mars importeras. Alla tidigare scheman, flygplatser och rörelser är oförändrade. V68: Returtrafik till Atlanta från Denver Stapleton, Houston Intercontinental/Hobby, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Ontario, Phoenix, San Diego, San Francisco och Seattle. 42 källrader på tryckta s. 71, 103, 124, 134, 193, 213, 214 och 222 ger 26 nya scheman och 57 rörelser. Tio anslutningar, fem genomgående rader med mellanstopp och DL68 LAX–ATL med start 2 mars enligt fotnot 6 på s. 135 hålls utanför. Alla tidigare scheman, flygplatser och rörelser är oförändrade. V69: Returtrafik till Atlanta från Kansas City, Minneapolis/St Paul, New Orleans, Oklahoma City, St Louis och Tulsa. 35 källrader på tryckta s. 117, 155, 170, 179, 206 och 238 ger 23 nya scheman och 47 rörelser. Tolv anslutningar via DFW/MEM hålls utanför. Alla tidigare scheman, flygplatser och rörelser är oförändrade. HNL24 X15 anländer nästa dag; ATL1140 till CVG anländer nästa dag. Alla tidigare data bevaras; flygplatsen CVG tillkommer. Tider och nonstoprader jämförda för sex franska Parisförbindelser. Tio ankomsttidskonflikter hålls utanför animationen; ingen AF-rörelse tillförs. Frankfurt–Marseille/Toulouse saknar nonstop-pil och importeras inte som direktsträckor. München placeras fortsatt vid Riem. V36 tillför sex nonstoprader / nio rörelser Tegel–Düsseldorf. SRAF/AFSR räknas en gång under första tryckta kod; SR763-raden från 11 februari används. V38 tillför fyra nonstoprader / åtta Wien–Paris-rörelser. AF använder CDG, OS använder Orly. Salzburg-raderna gäller torsdag/söndag och importeras inte i detta fönster. V39 tillför 65 nonstoprader / 96 Italien-rörelser. Linate och Pisa identifierade separat; AZ1351 delas i CDG–Genua och Genua–Neapel med 45 minuters uppehåll. V40 tillför två nonstoprader och två fredagsrörelser Orly–Warszawa/Okęcie och retur. notes.en: 55-page PDF advertised as complete by the archive; the entire pagination has not been audited and the source is provisionally treated as partial. Nordic non-stop rows visually reviewed. The VIA arrow means non-stop per page 4; day codes and local times per pages 2–4. Paris B/G means Charles de Gaulle, and Oslo explicitly means Fornebu. Only individually timed legs are imported. Edition 25 applies; subsequent amendments and actual operation are unverified. V25 adds four AFSK/SKAF rows linking Copenhagen with Nice/Lyon. Both codes are retained in the note; the first printed code is used for catalog grouping. Each departure is counted once; the actual operating carrier is undetermined. V28 adds Great Britain services linking Heathrow/Manchester with Paris, Lyon and Nice. December amendments and AFBA919 effective 1 March reviewed. BA-coded rows are grouped under British Airways. AFBA919 counted once under AF; actual operator undetermined. V29 adds EI522/EI523 and AF968/AF969 linking Dublin and Charles de Gaulle in both directions: four schedule rows, six movements. EI523 is valid through 28 March. Other Irish rows on these spreads do not operate Friday/Saturday and are not imported. V30 uses Air Inter no. 52 for IT day-dependent number prefixes. Times and non-stop rows compared for six French Paris links. Ten arrival-time conflicts withheld from animation; no AF movement added. V31 adds 42 non-stop rows with Spanish endpoints, 50 movements. AF/IB double codes counted once under first printed code. Rows without non-stop arrow, including Palma–Paris IB668/669 and Lyon–Madrid, excluded. Page 5 gives a Nice–Monaco frequency but no times; no such movements imported. V32 adds 15 reviewed rows and 15 Portugal movements. TP412* Porto–Paris retained as a candidate due to unresolved airport/terminal symbol and not animated. AF1440/1441 Lisbon–Lyon lack a non-stop arrow and are not imported as non-stop legs. V33 adds 22 reviewed rows and 35 Netherlands movements. Amsterdam–Marseille, KLAF306/307 Rotterdam–Paris and AF1910/1911 Nice–Amsterdam lack a non-stop arrow and are not imported as non-stop legs. AFKL/KLAF cooperation services counted once under the first printed airline code. V34 adds 24 reviewed rows and 31 Belgium movements. Brussels–Marseille lacks a non-stop arrow and is not imported as a non-stop leg. AFSN/SNAF cooperation services counted once under the first printed airline code. SNAF639 retains printed 08:01. V35 adds 56 reviewed rows and 89 West Germany movements. Rows effective 1 November used where indicated. Frankfurt–Marseille/Toulouse lack non-stop arrows and are not imported as non-stop legs. Munich remains located at Riem. V36 adds six non-stop rows / nine Tegel–Düsseldorf movements. AF766 does not continue to Tegel on Saturday per pages 32/62; the earlier Paris–Düsseldorf movement is retained. V37 adds 48 non-stop rows / 80 movements between Geneva/Zurich and France. SRAF/AFSR counted once under the first printed code; SR763 row effective 11 February used. V38 adds four non-stop rows / eight Vienna–Paris movements. AF uses CDG, OS uses Orly. Salzburg rows operate on Thursday/Sunday and are excluded from the window. V39 adds 65 non-stop rows / 96 Italy movements. Linate and Pisa identified separately; AZ1351 is split into CDG–Genoa and Genoa–Naples with a 45-minute ground interval. V40 adds two non-stop rows and two Friday movements between Orly and Warsaw/Okęcie. AFLO280/LOAF273 are each counted once; actual operator is not established. V41 adds six non-stop rows and six movements: two Prague–Orly and four Budapest–Orly. The selected Friday AFMA559 row is valid through 28 February. Every combined code is counted once. V42 adds eight non-stop rows and eight movements: three for Otopeni and five for Sofia, including two cargo flights. AF719 and AFLZ706 are through itineraries with intermediate stops on page 10 and are not imported as non-stop. Timed intermediate segments are missing. Combined codes are counted once. V43 adds eight non-stop rows and eight movements: four Belgrade–Orly and four Zagreb–Orly, half AF-coded and half JU-coded. Surčin and Pleso are explicitly named. Both belong to Yugoslavia in the 1986 country classification. V44 adds eleven non-stop rows/movements: ten Athens–France and one CDG–Larnaca. Friday AFOA600/601 are counted once under AF. Saturday AF600/601 and OA201/202 respect row validity. AF164 arrives next day after the window end but still overlaps the window. V45 adds six non-stop rows and eight Istanbul–Paris movements: AF608/609 Friday and Saturday, TK927/928 Friday and TK925/926 Saturday. B=CDG 2B and S=Orly. TK928 arrives next local day but on the same UTC date. Ankara connection rows are not imported as direct flights. V46 adds twelve movements with USSR endpoints, seven grouped under AF and five under SU. AF270 has two legs and a 75-minute Moscow stop. AFSU700 is counted once under AF and goes to Borispol, not Zhulyany. SU251/252 date 31/10 is a start date; applicable Friday AF720/721 variants start 7 February. V50: pages 76 and 88 corroborate times, operating days, airports and nonstop markings for 18 Air Inter rows/20 Paris–Strasbourg movements. Full IT numbers follow the own-edition Air Inter day-colour rule. The comparison creates no extra AF movements. V51: the Barcelona departure spread (printed pages 16–17) is absent from the reviewed PDF; PDF pages 9–10 jump from 14–15 to 18–19. Adjacent spreads and the whole-file page overview checked. No Barcelona return is created from inbound times. V123: 34 new separately timed Caribbean nonstop rows; date conditions and Paris A=CDG/S=Orly checked. Timetable, not confirmed operation.

notes.en: The archive dates this Southwest system timetable to 12 January 1986. AirTimes lists the next edition on 18 March 1986; no printed expiry date or complete set of amendments has been verified. Printed pages 13–16 were visually checked. Red flight numbers designate Southwest; blue Muse Air rows are excluded. The page footers define N/S as nonstop and days 1 Monday through 7 Sunday. All 235 red N/S rows in the Dallas section are transcribed, including rows producing no movement in the window. Times are interpreted as local under timetable convention and the Central/Mountain Time difference; a separate all-times-local legend has not been found. Local departure dates are limited to 27 February–1 March, with interval overlap selecting visible movements. Scheduled service, not confirmed operation, identified aircraft or actual flight paths. The rest of the network, Muse Air, intermediate stops in through services and subsequent amendments remain unreviewed. V59: Houston Hobby section, pages 20–24, reviewed. 116 additional red N/S rows to/from 12 destinations transcribed; 45 Dallas rows were already imported in v58. Blue Muse Air rows and intermediate-stop/connecting itineraries excluded. PHX uses America/Phoenix, UTC−7; El Paso UTC−7 and the other new endpoints UTC−6 on the import dates. WN797 and WN717 arrive on the next local day; Sunday WN956/997 rows produce no movements in the window. Airline coverage remains partial: other network sections, Muse Air, complete physical through-service chains and amendments remain unreviewed. V60: Phoenix pages 44–46 and Las Vegas pages 27–29 visually reviewed. 149 red N/S source rows transcribed: 132 new schedules, four previously imported Houston rows and 13 Phoenix–Las Vegas rows repeated in both city sections. Duplicates match flight number, endpoints, times, operating days and arrival-day offset. Tulsa–Phoenix is N/S; the reverse itineraries have an intermediate stop and are not imported as nonstop. Arizona/Mountain Time UTC−7, Pacific Time UTC−8, Central Time UTC−6. Phoenix–Las Vegas arrives five minutes earlier on the destination clock on the same calendar day, with a 55-minute elapsed timetable duration. Denver uses historical Stapleton, Las Vegas the McCarran name. Airline coverage remains partial; other network sections, complete through-service chains and amendments remain unreviewed. V61: Albuquerque pages 2–4 and El Paso pages 17–20 visually reviewed. 170 red N/S source rows: 94 new schedules, 65 previously imported rows, one corrected previous row and ten Albuquerque–El Paso rows repeated in both city sections. Flight 797 El Paso–Houston arrival corrected from 00:25 to 00:05 next day; pages 18 and 22 agree. This was an import transcription error, not conflicting sources. Houston–El Paso 736 has one stop and is not nonstop. Kansas City denotes MCI rather than downtown MKC. Airline coverage remains partial; remaining network sections, through-service chains and amendments need review. V62: Los Angeles pages 30–32, Ontario 43–44, San Diego 51–53, San Francisco 53–54, Chicago Midway 10–11, Kansas City 25–27, St. Louis 55–56, Little Rock 29–30 and Tulsa 56–58 visually reviewed. 244 red N/S source rows: 66 new schedules, 129 previously imported rows, two corrected previous rows and 47 repeats between city sections. WN703 LAX–PHX corrected to days 15 and WN717 SAN–PHX to 12345 according to matching counterpart pages. Corrections affect only weekdays outside the import dates and notes, not previous movement times or counts. Chicago denotes Midway, separate from O’Hare. IAH–Tulsa 20 is N/S; no nonstop return inferred. Airline coverage remains partial; other network sections, complete through-service chains, Muse Air and amendments remain unreviewed. V63: remaining city sections Amarillo, Austin, Corpus Christi, Denver, Houston Intercontinental, Lubbock, Midland/Odessa, New Orleans, Oklahoma City, Harlingen and San Antonio reviewed for red N/S rows. 358 source rows: 16 new schedules, 324 previously imported, two corrected previous and 16 repeats of new schedules. 32 new movements; one erroneous previous Saturday WN736 SAT–ELP movement removed. WN906 LBB–ABQ and WN736 SAT–ELP corrected to days 123457 according to both endpoint sections. WN939 LBB–Austin 23:00–00:00 arrives on the next calendar day. This city sweep does not verify actual operation, complete through-service chains, Muse Air or later amendments. Next major research lead: Delta February timetable.

notes.en: Dan-Air Winter 85/86, printed page 4: DA834, 12345.. (dot=no service), local time 09:45–11:00, Stops 0. Import limited to day 5 within 28 February–1 March 1986. Page 2 legend: 1=Monday, 7=Sunday; local times. Amsterdam and Berlin UTC+1, Bristol UTC. No return or onward timings inferred.
